finding.claim: When the verifier cache is enabled, a token that has exp but no iat is cached with a TTL of now + cacheTTL instead of its exp, so the token keeps being accepted for up to cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) after exp.
finding.source: A holder of a validly signed, short-lived token that has exp but no iat claim; the token must pass verification once while still unexpired.
finding.sink: Cache-hit return in verify() (src/verifier.js:368-377), which returns the cached payload without re-running the exp validator.

trace.note: verify() checks the cache before decoding; a hit returns the stored value without validators.
First verification path builds cacheContext with payload.
verifyToken runs the exp validator while the token is still unexpired, so the first call succeeds.
cacheSet is called with the success payload.
hasIat = typeof payload.iat === 'number' is false, so the block that records exp is skipped and cacheValue[2] stays 0.
maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL; with cacheValue[2] === 0 it is applied as the expiry.
On a later call after exp, min === 0 and now <= max hold, so the cache hit is returned and exp is never re-checked.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification runs before caching, so tokens cannot be forged (verifier.js:421-430, 454-471). Cache key is a full token hash (src/utils.js:45-59). Tokens with iat correctly record exp and cap TTL via Math.min (verifier.js:120-134). Error results are cached separately (verifier.js:110-115). Cache is only active when the cache option is truthy (verifier.js:606, createCache at verifier.js:83-86). Default cacheTTL is 600000 (verifier.js:499). Not executed: package.json and node_modules are absent, so this was verified by reading the code only.
